Subject: Processed interactions rights & subprocessor path — DPA ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — HealthBridge is interested in moving forward with a pilot but legal/procurement raised a few hard requirements before we can sign:

- An explicit contractual commitment that customer interactions (prompts + responses) will not be used to improve or retrain Redwood models unless we opt in.
- Clear ownership/entitlement language for prompt/response outputs (we need to ensure derivative rights stay with HealthBridge).
- A current subprocessor inventory with regions and whether they have access to raw prompts or aggregated telemetry.
- Evidence of technical controls (routing, non-learning model variants, retention policies, KMS residency).

We've attached a one-page DPA request summary for your legal team (HealthBridge_DPA_request_20261121.pdf). If Redwood can provide an operational attestation and a redline of the DPA with the above commitments, we can prioritize this in our procurement queue.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Alex Torres

Marissa / Priyom — quick legal take and proposed language items. I drafted a short redline and included operational evidence we should provide.

Key legal asks to include in redline (high level):
- "No Model Improvement" clause: Redwood will not use Customer Inputs (prompts), Outputs (responses), or derived representations to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any model used to serve Customer, unless Customer provides prior written consent.
- Output entitlement: Customer retains all rights to Outputs generated from Customer Inputs; Redwood will not assert ownership or sell aggregated derivatives.
- Subprocessor transparency: list of subprocessors with role, country, and whether they handle unredacted prompts.
- Data transfer safeguards: standard SCCs (if EU transfers), onshore KMS options, and optional localized storage lanes.

Operational evidence to attach:
- Current subprocessor_inventory_20261121.xlsx (name/role/region/access level).
- Ops attestation (ops-no-train-attestation.txt) describing routing to non-improving variants and retention SLA.
- Reference to SOC2 + recent penetration test summary (we can provide SOC2 cert).

I've added the redline to redlined-dpa-marissa-v1.pdf and flagged three negotiable baskets: (1) absolute prohibition vs. opt-in model-improvement, (2) granularity of output entitlements (tenant vs. aggregated), (3) remedies / audit rights.

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Alex — quick ops/technical evidence to address your procurement points. Below is a concise summary (I can share a fuller runbook link once NDA/contract stage is OK):

1) Isolation for opt-out:
- We serve two logical variants for many models: "production-learning" (default) and "production-nolearn" (no model-improvement). HealthBridge traffic can be pinned to the production-nolearn variant via routing policy at the request header level.
- Routing is enforced in the control plane and logged; there is no background ingestion from production-nolearn into training pipelines.

2) Subprocessor access:
- See attached subprocessor_inventory_20261121.xlsx. It includes columns: name, role, country, handles_raw_prompts (yes/no). By default, subprocessors used for telemetry/metrics do not receive raw prompt text; only our onshore S3 cluster ("redwood-data-us") holds raw prompt blobs for customers that opt in.

3) Retention / caches:
- KV/prefix cache: ephemeral, max TTL 2 hours, default 30 minutes for interactive sessions.
- Request logs: full request+response logs retained for 30 days in our primary logs for debugging; can be configured to 7 days for enterprise pilot.
- Long-term telemetry (token counts, latencies) is aggregated and stored without raw prompt text by default.

4) KMS / residency:
- KMS keys can be customer-managed (BYOK) in AWS us-west-2. We offer an EU-only KMS lane on request.

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_20261121.xlsx, ops-no-train-attestation.txt

If you want a copy of the runbook or the routing policy examples, I'll drop a restricted Drive link once the procurement channel confirms receipt. Happy to join the legal/tech sync.
